description: Makes a first assembly edit from the plan and the take log, as a file your own editing software opens: OpenTimelineIO (otio), FCPXML (fcpxml), a CMX 3600 edit decision list (edl) or an ALE log (ale). It puts the chosen takes in story order, each as long as the plan's slot (a shot with no usable take is left as a gap and listed in the report), linked by your human's own file names so they relink to footage on their own drives. No media is uploaded to us and none comes back; no AI model runs. Input: plan; takes (a dpl.takes/1 log); format (otio, fcpxml, edl or ale); optionally fps (24, 25, 23.976 or 29.97, a number or text; 24 if left out), drop_frame (true or false), media_root (the folder the footage is in, for relinking) and sync_sound (true by default). Output: {format, media_type, file_name, content, report, more_files?}. Save content as file_name. report lists the files to relink, the gaps, any warnings and what the chosen format cannot carry; an EDL is one file for each track, so any further files are in more_files, in order. We don't keep the plan or the take log. Needs an agent key from a Shoot Plan account, and is free up to 3 projects a month. A project is identified by the plan's work id and title; it counts when this tool first makes a finished document for it that month. shoot_plan_allowance says what is left. Over the limit it answers ALLOWANCE_REACHED: do not retry, a new key will not help, tell your human. A fair-use limit also applies: up to 20 finished-document calls for any one project and 60 for the account each month. To count projects we keep, against your account, a one-way fingerprint (hash) of the project's id and title, the month, how many finished documents were made and when, for 13 months after the end of that month. Plans up to 8 MB and 120 calls a minute (5,000 a day).

fps.description: Frame rate: 24, 25, 23.976 or 29.97 (a number or text). Optional.

media_root.description: Optional: the folder the footage is in, for relinking.

plan.description: The plan itself: a dpl.plan/1 JSON object (not text inside a string). Call shoot_plan_format for the schema links and an example.

sync_sound.description: Optional: include sync sound where the log has it. Default true.

takes.description: The take log: a dpl.takes/1 JSON object, {format, work_id, takes: [...]}. Each take has op_id, shot (the plan's shot id), kind and verdict; file names and timecodes are optional. A take log holds text about recordings: the tools take no video or audio.

name: shoot_plan_export_edit
title: Export the chosen takes as an edit for your editing software
